title: SQL string concatenation — review required
description: Building a SQL statement with + concatenation lets input characters become query syntax (SQL injection). This lexical rule cannot prove the concatenated value is untrusted — treat every hit as review-required, not as proven exploitable.
remediation: Use parameterized queries (placeholders with bound values) so SQL structure stays separate from data. Never concatenate input into query text, including table or column names — allowlist those.
limitation: Lexical: any + inside a query(/execute( call matches, including arithmetic on trusted numbers. Calls without concatenation are out of scope for this rule.

tests.line: db.query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = " + id)
db.execute('DELETE FROM t WHERE n = ' + name)
